claims.text: Sparse, filamentous neurons and substantial noise make 3D fluorescence microscopy segmentation difficult; limited receptive fields in sliding-window inference hinder long-range morphology modeling and can produce fragmented masks.

NeuroRefiner iteratively combines global inspection, region-specific instruction generation, TopoRefineNet editing, and validation of local refinements; it stops when morphology is judged complete or the maximum iteration count is reached.

The Global Inspector uses global and patch-level mask projections together with the zeroth Betti number, computed as the connected-component count in each corresponding 3D region, to identify blocks with false-positive or false-negative errors.
The Refinement Advisor compares image and mask projections in the xy and yz planes and generates instructions specifying both a spatial location and an editing operation.

The main method description requires the Change Validator to check instruction adherence and topological improvement, retrying failed edits with new instructions and escalating persistently unresolved blocks to human experts.

TopoRefineNet encodes the concatenated image and noisy mask, embeds instructions with a frozen pretrained text encoder, and fuses text with the deepest visual features using cross-attention before decoding a refined mask.
TopoRefineNet uses two training stages: synthetic morphological defects with perturbation-derived instructions, followed by real segmentation errors with instructions synthesized using Qwen3-VL.

Evaluation uses BigNeuron, CWMBS, and ZBFWB with previously established training–testing splits. BigNeuron contains expert-annotated neurons from multiple species and imaging platforms; CWMBS includes 83 strong-noise and 162 weak-signal volumes of 256×256×256 voxels at 0.2×0.2×1 µm resolution.
ZBFWB contains confocal images from 6-day-old zebrafish larvae, with dimensions of 1000×2000×250 voxels and resolution of 0.5×0.5×1 µm.
The second training stage selects 5,310 error-containing volumes of 128×128×64 voxels from predictions by 3D U-Net, V-Net, UNETR, nnFormer, and SwinUNETR, using connected-component and F1 scores.
Experiments use Qwen3-VL-8B for all agents, Qwen3 Embedding 0.6B for text embeddings, 128×128-pixel inspection regions, and a maximum of 5 iterations.
On ZBFWB, NeuroRefiner initialized from 3D U-Net achieves F1 of 86.13%, compared with 72.94% for 3D U-Net and 83.11% for GBP-Net: gains of 13.19 and 3.02 percentage points, respectively.
On BigNeuron, NeuroRefiner achieves F1 of 90.05%, SSD of 6.94, and MES of 72.02, compared with 86.33%, 11.27, and 66.82 for its 3D U-Net initialization.

On CWMBS, refining 3D U-Net masks increases F1 from 74.94% to 90.07% on weak-signal volumes and from 79.23% to 86.37% on strong-noise volumes; refining nnUNet masks yields F1 of 91.85% and 84.84%, respectively.
In agent ablations, the full system achieves F1 of 86.13% on ZBFWB and 88.83% on CWMBS, versus 76.39% and 79.96% when TopoRefineNet refines all blocks without agents.

Training only on real defects from scratch increases the Change Validator rejection rate by a reported 23.57% and degrades F1 by a reported 1.17% on ZBFWB and 1.89% on CWMBS relative to two-stage training.

NeuroRefiner's 2D maximum-intensity projections lose depth information in dense regions, hindering precise 3D error localization; neuron overlap can also interfere with inspection of some complex volumes.

The authors present NeuroRefiner as the first LLM-based multi-agent system for topology-aware iterative neuron segmentation optimization, and contribute TopoRefineNet with a two-stage training strategy for instruction-guided structural editing.
The framework performs progressive refinement without agent training and exposes diagnostic decisions and editing instructions for auditing.
